topicDisplay: Area D The World Of Work
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: How do you say “My dream is to become a lawyer”?
questions.explain: “Hacerse” = “to become” and “abogado” = “lawyer”, so “Mi sueño es hacerme abogado”.

questions.q: What does “aprobar un examen” mean?
questions.explain: “Aprobar” means “to pass”; to fail is “suspender”.

questions.q: Which sentence means “I work as a waiter at the weekend”?
options: Trabaja de camarero los fines de semana
Trabajo de camarero los fines de semana
Trabajo de cartero los fines de semana
questions.explain: “De camarero” = as a waiter and “los fines de semana” = at the weekend.

questions.q: Which means “The pay is low but I enjoy the work”?
options: El sueldo es alto pero disfruto del trabajo
El suelo es bajo pero disfruto del trabajo
El sueldo es bajo pero odio el trabajo
El sueldo es bajo pero disfruto del trabajo
questions.explain: “El sueldo es bajo” = the pay is low and “disfruto del trabajo” = I enjoy the work.

questions.q: Which sentence means 'I have to revise for my exams'?
options: Tengo que repasar para mis exámenes
Tengo que faltar a mis exámenes
questions.explain: 'Repasar' means 'to revise' and 'tener que' = 'to have to', so this means 'I have to revise for my exams'.

questions.q: Which sentence means “I find maths difficult”?
questions.explain: “Me resultan difíciles” = “I find them difficult”; the verb agrees with the plural “las matemáticas”.

questions.q: What does “el director” mean in a school context?
questions.explain: At school “el director” means “the headteacher/principal”.

questions.q: What does “ganarse la vida” mean?
questions.explain: “Ganarse la vida” is an idiom meaning “to earn a living”.

questions.q: What does 'el billete de ida y vuelta' mean?
questions.explain: 'Ida y vuelta' means 'there and back', so 'el billete de ida y vuelta' = 'a return ticket'.

questions.q: What does “el recreo” mean?
questions.explain: “El recreo” means “break/recess” at school.

questions.q: How would you write 'trabajador' to describe a hard-working woman?
questions.explain: Adjectives ending in -dor add -a for the feminine singular, so a hard-working woman is 'trabajadora'.

questions.q: What does 'el éxito' mean?
questions.explain: 'El éxito' is a false friend: it means 'success', not 'exit' (which is 'la salida').

questions.q: What does “la empresa” mean?
questions.explain: “La empresa” means “a company/firm”; it is a false friend with English “enterprise/promise”.

questions.q: What does “las prácticas laborales” mean?
questions.explain: “Las prácticas laborales” means “work experience / a work placement”.

questions.q: Which means “I would earn more money if I spoke languages”?
options: Ganaría más dinero si hablo idiomas
Ganaré más dinero si hablara idiomas
Gano más dinero si hablo idiomas
Ganaría más dinero si hablara idiomas
questions.explain: An unreal condition uses conditional + imperfect subjunctive: “ganaría... si hablara”.

questions.q: How do you say “I would like to be a vet”?
questions.explain: “Veterinario” = vet and “me gustaría ser” = I would like to be.

questions.q: What does “la tarea” mean?
questions.explain: “La tarea” means “a task / homework” (also “los deberes”).

questions.q: What does “el desempleo” mean?
questions.explain: “El desempleo” means “unemployment” (also “el paro”).

questions.q: What does “suspender” mean in school Spanish?
questions.explain: “Suspender” means “to fail” an exam; it is a false friend with English “suspend”.

questions.q: What does 'el desempleo' mean?
questions.explain: 'El desempleo' (also 'el paro') means 'unemployment'; 'el empleo' is 'employment/a job'.

questions.q: What does “el bombero” mean?
questions.explain: “El bombero” means “a firefighter”.

questions.q: What does “la nota” mean in “mi nota de inglés”?
questions.explain: In school Spanish “la nota” means “the mark/grade”.
